_comment: Fragment 61 — D-106: the negative fixtures were never in the repository; three defects introduced by the pass that found five; Lane B assessed as ready. Merged 2026-08-24.

nodes.label: D-106 — The Fixtures Were Never in the Repository
nodes.description: The fifth critic pass, on a separate turn against the fourth. Five findings, none dismissed, three of them introduced by the pass under review.
nodes.rationale: Every recorded pass has found defects in the one before it, and the ratio of self-inflicted findings has not improved across five consecutive recordings.

nodes.label: The Record of the Test Outlived the Test
nodes.description: Fourteen claims that a check had been negative-tested, with no fixture anywhere in the repository. Each suite ran once in a session scratchpad and what survived was the sentence saying it passed.
nodes.rationale: The closure file went further and told the reader to run a fixture from that scratchpad — a reproduction instruction pointing outside the repository, inside the section whose entire purpose is reproducibility.

nodes.label: The Defence Against Ceremonial Checks Was Itself Unverifiable
nodes.description: The consistency suite proves the checks pass on a healthy repository. The fixtures are the only evidence they fail on an unhealthy one, and that is the property every claim in the register rests on.
nodes.rationale: A check that cannot fail is recorded five separate times as a named failure mode here, and the only thing standing against it could not be re-run by anyone but its author, once.

nodes.label: A Fixture Asserts the Finding, Not Merely a Failure
nodes.description: Each fixture matches the intended message rather than accepting any failure, opens its suite with an unmutated positive control, and restores the working tree in a finally block.
nodes.rationale: A check failing for the wrong reason satisfies a naive fixture, and this apparatus has produced that exact defect twice. A suite with no green case proves only that a check can fail, never that it can pass.

nodes.label: The Fixtures Found a Defect in Themselves on Their First Tracked Run
nodes.description: Porting one fixture out of the scratchpad turned a narrow assertion about one entry being silenced into a wrong one about a different entry appearing. It reported a miss rather than passing quietly.
nodes.rationale: The corrected assertion has to claim both halves, because no findings at all would be satisfied by a disabled gate rather than a satisfied one.

nodes.label: A Gate That Blocks on Its Own Failure
nodes.description: A parse failure was read as no declaration, which blocks a correctly declared crossing and turns a tooling failure into a work stoppage.
nodes.rationale: The fallback replicates the rule rather than abandoning it or reverting to the whole message body, which would restore the defect the previous pass removed, and it announces itself so a degraded run is visible.

nodes.label: A Required Field With No Answerable Value
nodes.description: One decision made a turn report mandatory; an earlier one defined the phase field as naming whoever owns the correction. A report on your own turn is not a correction, so the required field had nothing to give it.
nodes.rationale: Two decisions each internally consistent produced an artifact that could not be written without guessing. A turn report now carries the reporting lane's own phase.

nodes.label: A Procedure That Existed Only in Memory
nodes.description: Two sprint boundaries had been performed and there was no written procedure for one. Both had defects and neither was hard.
nodes.rationale: The written steps mark the unenforceable ones as unenforceable, so a green mechanical check is never read as evidence that the meaning-carrying half was performed.
